title: Model Bridge Marketplace: Warm-Capacity Subscriptions — Product Brief & PRD
author: Elena Rodriguez
content:
Summary:

This document defines the product brief, high-level PRD, design constraints, pricing constructs, and launch plan for the Model Bridge Marketplace Warm-Capacity Subscriptions. The feature introduces a marketplace of third-party and Redwood-verified model variants where customers can purchase warm-reserved execution capacity in subscription bands that attach to model SKUs. The goal is to provide lower cold-start latency, predictable cost for heavy callers, and a commercial path to monetize curated variants with managed warm capacity.

Background and Problem Statement:

- Customers using model variants (open or partner models) encounter two friction points: variable cold-start latency for spiky traffic and opaque unit economics across variant and capacity choices.
- Enterprise customers have expressed willingness to pay for predictable latency and throughput guarantees for specific model variants used in core product flows.
- There is no single product that combines a marketplace (variant discovery + licensing) with an attached, metered warm-capacity subscription offering and a clear UX for developer selection and routing.

Value Proposition:

- For Developers: simple discovery and one-click attach of warm-capacity plans to a model variant with client SDK flags and telemetry hooks for preflight checks.
- For Platform/Operators: improved capacity predictability and autoscaling smoothing via long-lived reservations; better ability to schedule heavy-tail workloads onto dedicated pools.
- For Redwood: new recurring revenue from subscription bands, increased adoption of curated variants, and reduced tail latency incidents.

Goals and Non-Goals (success criteria):

Goals:
1. Deliver warm-capacity attach UX and billing for model variants (MVP) within Q4 2026.
2. Achieve 50% reduction in cold-start tail (95th percentile) for customers using subscriptions vs baseline.
3. Secure at least 5 pilot customers on paid plans within 90 days post-launch.

Non-Goals:
- This PRD does not include a full decentralized billing marketplace or revenue split automation for third parties in MVP (commercial reconciliation will be manual).
- It does not replace Dedicated reserved GPU contracts. Warm capacity is a software reservation layer on top of Hosted pools.

User Personas and Journeys:

- Small SaaS Engineer (Self-serve): discovers a high-performance summarization variant in the marketplace, attaches a Bronze warm band, toggles preflight checks in SDK, and validates latency improvements in Console.
- Platform SRE: maps warm subscriptions to a predictable capacity class; uses Console dashboards to see warm utilization and make scheduling changes.
- Revenue Ops: validates invoices and reconciles marketplace partner payouts (manual for MVP).

PRD — Requirements (MUST/HIGH/MED/LOW):

MUST:
- Marketplace listing model variant metadata: name, version, memory footprint, token throughput estimate, certified latency profile (cold and warm), and vendor attribution.
- Subscription SKU model: tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold) with defined reserved concurrency, soft headroom, and expected 95p tail latency improvement.
- Attach API: endpoint to attach/detach a subscription to a tenant+route (REST + SDK). Example payload:

POST /v1/marketplace/attach
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "tenant_id": "acct_123",
  "route_id": "payments-summarize",
  "variant_sku": "open-summarizer-v2-gold",
  "subscription_sku": "warm-gold-100"
}

- Routing policy: requests matching a route with an attached warm subscription must preferentially route to warm pools; on exhaustion, fallback to recommended compatible variants with documented SLA degradation.
- Billing integration: capture subscription SKU, start/end timestamps, and pro-rated charges for partial periods into the billing ledger.

HIGH:
- Console UI: discovery catalog, attach flow, warm-capacity utilization graph (per-tenant, per-variant).
- Telemetry: preflight latency probe and gateway metrics that tag requests as Warm vs Cold.
- Alerts: when warm subscription utilization exceeds 85% for >15m.

MED:
- Automated partner revenue split UI for future integration (data model only in MVP).
- SDK helper that toggles warm-only routing for test mode.

LOW:
- Allow customers to self-serve nominee partner payouts and reconciliations.

Design Spec — Architecture Overview:

Key components (MVP):
- Marketplace Catalog Service (catalogsvc): stores variant metadata, SKU definitions, pricing. Exposes read APIs for Console and SDK.
- Subscription Manager (submgr): authoritative ledger of tenant subscriptions, entitlements, and soft-headroom config. Integrates with Billing Service for charges.
- Warm Pool Orchestrator (wpo): maps subscriptions to warm pool capacity classes and ensures pool reservation via scheduling hints.
- Routing Gate (router): runtime decision point that prefers warm pools when entitlement exists and enforces fallback policies.
- Console UX and SDK feature flags.

Data Contracts and Example JSONs:

Variant metadata example:
{
  "variant_sku": "open-summarizer-v2-gold",
  "model_name": "open-summarizer-v2",
  "memory_gb": "24",
  "throughput_tps": "18",
  "certified_warm_95p_latency_ms": "120",
  "certified_cold_95p_latency_ms": "800",
  "vendor": "OpenCommunity",
  "compatible_hardware": ["A100-40GB","H100-80GB"]
}

Subscription SKU table (text table):
| SKU | Reserved concurrency | Soft headroom | Target 95p warm latency | Monthly list price (USD) |
|-----|----------------------|---------------|-------------------------|--------------------------|
| warm-bronze-10 | 10 | +2 | 250ms | $1,200 |
| warm-silver-50 | 50 | +5 | 160ms | $5,000 |
| warm-gold-100 | 100 | +12 | 120ms | $9,000 |

SLOs and metrics to track (MVP):
- Warm 95p latency per variant and per tenant — target per SKU declared in catalog.
- Warm subscription utilization: % of reserved concurrency utilized over sliding 5m and 1h windows.
- Warm fallback rate: fraction of requests that fell back to non-warm due to exhaustion. Target: <5% for normal operation.

Operational Runbook Excerpts (On-call SRE):

1) Symptom: Console shows warm-subscription utilization >95% for >30m and multiple tenants report increased cold starts.
   - Step 1: Identify impacted warm pool and check "wpo" scheduling backlog. CLI: curl -s https://internal-api/wpo/pools?pool_id=<pool>
   - Step 2: Temporarily increase soft headroom for affected subscriptions (submgr API) and notify customers.
   - Step 3: If scheduling backlog persists >1h, trigger capacity bump playbook (see Runbooks/terraform-and-iac).

2) Symptom: Billing records missing subscription start events.
   - Step 1: Check submgr write-ahead log for recent failed transactions.
   - Step 2: Reconcile with Console attach audit events and create manual invoice if necessary. Owner: Revenue Ops.

Security and Compliance Considerations:

- Marketplace listings must include allowed-data-usage flags and required contract attachments for partner-owned variants. Any variant flagged "restricted" must not be discoverable by public tenant catalogs.
- Audit logs for attach/detach operations must be retained for 13 months (complies with existing retention policy).

Roadmap & Milestones (high-level):

1) Q4 2026 (MVP): Catalog read/write, subscription attach API, routing preference to warm pools, billing capture (manual reconciliation), Console attach flow (beta). Pilot with up to 5 customers.
2) Q1 2027: Partner revenue split automation, Console warm utilization dashboards, SDK helpers, partner onboarding guide.
3) Q2 2027: Dynamic price bands, auto-scale warm-headroom based on seasonality signals, per-route fidelity negotiation with warm-aware fallback.

Pricing and Packaging:

Pricing principles:
- Simple predictable bands that map to developer mental models (Bronze/Silver/Gold).
- List price includes a committed monthly fee for reserved concurrency; overage pricing is per-request at a discounted hosted token rate.
- Enterprise customers can negotiate dedicated bundles and private warm allocations (out-of-scope for MVP billing automation).

Example pricing scenarios (text table):
| Customer | Variant | Reserved | Monthly | Expected unit cost improvement |
| Acme Inc | open-summarizer-v2 | 50 (silver) | $5,000 | ~30% lower per-token latency cost at 95p |
| RetailCo | vendor-qa-v1 | 10 (bronze) | $1,200 | improved UX for checkout summaries |

Commercial notes for Sales and Revenue Ops:
- Pilot pricing will include a 3-month discounted rate at 50% list for early adopters.
- Revenue Ops will manually reconcile partner payouts in MVP; contracts must be attached before listing is published.

Launch Checklist (MVP):
- [ ] Catalog CRUD endpoints implemented and documented.
- [ ] Subscription attach/detach API + SDK wrappers.
- [ ] Router changes deployed behind feature flag.
- [ ] Billing ledger capture and invoice test harness.
- [ ] Console attach flow + warm-utilization widget (beta).
- [ ] Pilot onboarding doc and partner contract template.
- [ ] Runbook added to eng-platform/runbooks.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Feature flag gated end-to-end flows exist and are exercised by automated e2e tests covering attach->route->billing paths.
- Pilot tenants report a measurable 95p latency improvement vs baseline for at least 3 variant SKUs.
- Billing records appear in ledger for each attach action within 5 minutes.

Release Notes (Draft for internal release):

Model Bridge Marketplace — Warm-Capacity Subscriptions (Internal Beta) — 2026-11-01
- Introduces marketplace catalog and subscription SKU model with attach API.
- Adds routing preference for warm subscriptions and console attach UX (beta).
- Billing ledger capture enabled for subscription SKUs (manual reconciliation).
- Known limitations: partner payouts are manual; autoscaling warm-headroom not yet implemented.

Open Risks and Mitigations:
- Risk: Warm pool overcommit leading to higher-than-expected fallbacks. Mitigation: conservative defaults on soft headroom and 85% utilization alerting.
- Risk: Confusion between Dedicated and Warm subscriptions. Mitigation: Console UX education, rename terms internally in docs.

Appendix — Example CLI snippets and SDK flags:

Attach via CLI (example):
redwood marketplace attach \
  --tenant acct_123 \
  --route payments-summarize \
  --variant open-summarizer-v2-gold \
  --sku warm-silver-50

SDK preflight example (python):
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="x")
client.marketplace.attach_preflight(route="payments-summarize", variant="open-summarizer-v2-gold")

Document links and further reading:
- See Console mockups in the design repository and Pilot onboarding checklist in /product-docs/roadmap-and-themes.

This product brief is intended to be the single source of truth for the Model Bridge warm-capacity pilot. Revisions will be tracked and reviewers listed above will sign off before GA.
